title: Fix crash on closed generic structs from referenced assemblies

lines.text: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).

Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.

requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement.intent: A [MessagePackObject] type with a member whose type is a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly must build cleanly and still get a generated resolver.

functional.text: The generator does not throw when a member's type is a closed generic struct or record struct defined in a referenced assembly.
The analyzer does not throw for the same member types.
The compiling assembly gets its generated resolver, as it does when the generic type is declared in the same project.

nonFunctional.text: A failure of the generator or analyzer must not pass silently as a build warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver. (inferred)
Behaviour for generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same project does not change. (inferred)

expectedBehaviours: Compiling a project with a [MessagePackObject] type that has a member typed as a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly (for example ValueTuple-like or a library GenericStruct<int>) does not make the source generator throw an IndexOutOfRangeException.
The same holds when the referenced generic value type is a record struct.
No CS8785 generator-failed warning or error is reported for these member types.

expectedBehaviours: Running the MessagePack analyzers on a [MessagePackObject] type whose member is a closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly does not throw IndexOutOfRangeException.
No AD0001 analyzer-crashed diagnostic is reported for that code.
Analyzer diagnostics that apply to the type are still reported as normal, and no spurious ones appear.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a closed generic struct member from a referenced metadata assembly checks that no AD0001 and no unexpected MsgPack diagnostics are produced.

expectedBehaviours: The consuming assembly gets a generated resolver and a formatter for the [MessagePackObject] type, as it does when the generic struct is declared in the same project.
At runtime, the generated resolver serializes and deserializes the object with the cross-assembly generic struct member without error.

A successful build is never missing the expected generated resolver.
expectedTests: Generator tests fail when the generator reports exceptions or generator-failure diagnostics, so a silent warning cannot pass.

story.what: The TypeCollector now wraps the analyzer's diagnostic callback so that a diagnostic is reported only when its location is in source and in a syntax tree of the compilation being analyzed. Two diagnostic sites that indexed DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] directly now use FirstOrDefault or a new null-safe helper, GetPropertyIdentifierLocation. The handling of [IgnoreMember] fields changes from |= to &= on nonPublicMembersAreSerialized. New tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata-only image and check that a consuming project using a closed generic struct or record struct from it builds with no diagnostics and gets its resolver; README and MsgPack004 docs gain short sections on types from referenced assemblies.
story.why: Types from a referenced assembly have no syntax references. When a member's type was a closed generic struct from metadata, indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] threw IndexOutOfRangeException in both the generator and the analyzer. The generator failure showed up only as a CS8785 warning, and the assembly was left without a generated resolver (MP-2283).

touches.note: reportDiagnostic is now a wrapper that calls ReportIfLocatedInCompilation when an analyzer callback is supplied.
New. Forwards a diagnostic only if its location is in source and in a syntax tree of this compilation.
New null-safe helper that returns the property identifier location, or null for metadata properties.
BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull and the field MemberNeedsKey no longer index DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]. The ignored-field flag update changes from |= to &=.
New helper. Compiles the defining source to a metadata image, runs the verifier, then runs the generator directly and asserts the resolver hint name is produced.
New tests for a struct, a record struct, and a struct with an unkeyed member.

findings.title: Ignored-field flag update changed from |= to &=
findings.detail: In the field loop of GetObjectInfo, the update for [IgnoreMember] fields changed from |= to &=, and the requirement does not ask for this. The flag starts as false, so a non-public ignored field can no longer set it. A public ignored field now clears it, even after an earlier non-public keyed member set it to true. The property branch at line 899 still uses |=, so properties and fields now behave differently. Clearing the flag skips the deferred non-public diagnostics, MessagePackObjectAllowPrivateRequired (line 1352) and the PartialTypeRequired check (line 1382). The generator could then emit a nested formatter into a non-partial type that has private keyed members, and the generated code would not compile. This breaks N2: behaviour for types declared in the same project changes.

findings.title: Positional record property diagnostic is now silently dropped
findings.detail: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null when the declaring syntax is not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax. For a positional record property, the syntax is a ParameterSyntax, even though the property is in source. The unkeyed-member path at lines 925-926 handles ParameterSyntax. With this change, BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull on a positional record parameter (for example [property: Key(null)]) gets a null location, and ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops it without reporting anything. The old code threw InvalidCastException here. The new code hides a valid diagnostic for a type in the current project instead of reporting it, which goes against N1 and N2.

citations.quote: var identifier = (syntax as PropertyDeclarationSyntax)?.Identifier ?? (syntax as ParameterSyntax)?.Identifier;

findings.title: Generated resolver output for cross-assembly struct is not verified
findings.detail: The new tests set SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck and only check that the resolver hint name is among the generated sources. No snapshot checks the resolver and formatter generated for a closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly. No round-trip test serializes and deserializes an instance through the generated resolver. F3 says the output must match the same-project case, and nothing in the change shows that the generated formatter is correct or compiles into working code.

findings.title: Generator or analyzer failures can still pass silently as build warnings
findings.detail: N1 asks that a generator or analyzer failure must not pass silently as a warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver. The change fixes the specific crash, and only the new tests treat warnings as failures. Nothing in the product makes a CS8785 or AD0001 failure surface as a build error or an error-level diagnostic. In addition, ReportIfLocatedInCompilation now drops any diagnostic without an in-compilation location without reporting it. If a type from a referenced assembly has problems that its defining assembly never reported (for example a NuGet package built without the analyzer), the consuming build stays silent.

refusals.reason: The README and the MsgPack004 help page now document a new contract: diagnostics about members of types from referenced assemblies are reported only by the defining assembly and are suppressed in the consuming project, and the code enforces this.
